- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates downside risk; add downward buffer or adjust for volatility clustering.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; apply dampening factor or limit upward momentum.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., price drops after peak or rebounds after trough), model often fails to recognize it; adjust for recent volatility or use moving average smoothing.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early periods (e.g., 2022-11-25) when sentiment is rising; anchor forecast to 10-15 day moving average.
- When sentiment shifts abruptly (e.g., from bullish to bearish), model often lags; adjust forecast horizon to reflect sentiment change within 3-5 days.
- If true outcome deviates >5% from forecast in first 5 days, model is likely overconfident; reduce forecast slope or add volatility penalty.
